messages.Bend the knees a little and allow the hi: Bend the knees a little and allow the hips to move back slightly while both feet stay grounded. Do not seek a deep seat or a fixed thigh angle.
messages.Bend the knees a little, tilt the pelvis: Bend the knees a little, tilt the pelvis and fold forward with a long back until the hands reach the chair seat or blocks. The head stays above the hips; there is no head-to-floor goal.
messages.Bend the knees clearly and hinge forward: Bend the knees clearly and hinge forward from the hips only as far as is comfortable. Rest the hands on the shins, the thighs or the chair seat. Holding the big toes is the traditional form and is not required.
messages.Bend the knees, slide feet down the wall: Bend the knees, slide feet down the wall and roll sideways before using hands to sit.
messages.Bend the raised knee before placing its: Bend the raised knee before placing its foot down, then roll sideways to leave; never swing legs behind the head in this course.
messages.Bend the right knee only as far as it st: Bend the right knee only as far as it stays above the ankle, not past the toes. Lean the trunk and rest the right forearm on the right thigh.
messages.Bending knees alone does not establish u: Bending knees alone does not establish unloading: neither leg may still be resting its weight on the support. messages.Existing Hatha h01 (boundaries), h02 (na: Existing Hatha h01 (boundaries), h02 (natural breath), h04 (supported seat), h19/h20/h23 (supported floor sitting/bound angle/forward reach), h29 (rest) and h35 (unhurried transitions) provide relevant foundations. Review the concepts; completing all Hatha or buying external lessons is not required. h35 alone does not teach a detailed floor transfer. Getting down/up, sitting and, where needed, side/back lying must be familiar movements the person can already perform comfortably that day. Do not attempt a first floor transfer from this text. If uncertain, choose chair observation/the knowledge task and resolve the gap with appropriate teaching support; app ticks cannot grant permission. This general pathway cannot decide suitability where personal limits, recent injury, pregnancy or health circumstances are uncertain. Pregnancy may require changes to prolonged stillness and back lying; a reclining lesson is not an automatic alternative. Discuss individual needs with a health professional and a suitably experienced yoga teacher. This proposal requires no fee, purchased certificate or particular provider. Prepare a mat on a level nonslip floor, a low firm folded blanket, a firm cushion/bolster, thigh supports if needed and a thin head support. A soft bed/sofa does not replace the floor surface. Props must not wobble, tip or slide; avoid tall loose stacks. Try the arrangement outside the pose. Keep the phone and optional timer accessible without reaching; do not fix your gaze on a screen. Select a familiar neutral rest and way off the floor beforehand. For chair observation use a sound four-legged non-wheeled chair; do not imitate floor poses on it. Let breathing follow its ordinary rhythm: no deepening, slowing, retention or matching seconds. The first entry/exit rehearsal is a brief trial, not a completed Yin hold. If setup is comfortable and the exit is known, you may choose to stay for up to about one minute; leaving earlier is always valid. In a later comfortable session you may choose up to two minutes; more time or depth is not a progression requirement. Do not deepen during the same hold in this introduction. A timer reminds you of an upper limit, not an endurance target. Eyes may remain open. When attention wanders, return to contact/ordinary breathing without pulling yourself into a model appearance. Only for a symptom-free setup/attention error: leave the pose; pause in neutral; choose one change; make a brief entry/exit rehearsal in a smaller form; compare support, ordinary breathing and exit before/after. One retest is enough; if unresolved, omit movement and record the uncertainty. If a prop moved, leave fully before resetting it; do not pull a loaded cushion away. Symptoms are not a correction drill. The learner can explain this introduction's Yin approach in their own words; plan support, entry, exit and an early stop; and select a short practice using at least two different taught shapes whose suitability has separately been established. In a new case they distinguish stopping for symptoms from an ordinary setup error. In a later separate session they recall the plan without the text and correct omissions. A physical skill claim additionally requires appropriate observation of actual entry, waiting and exit in those two shapes. Someone completing explanation alone records the knowledge outcome, not a completed physical outcome. Lesson ticks, long holds or large angles do not prove this endpoint.

messages.From mountain, step wide, turn the front: From mountain, step wide, turn the front foot toward the mat end and turn the rear toes slightly inward before bending either knee.
messages.From mountain, use a chair-supported fol: From mountain, use a chair-supported fold and pause before moving to tabletop or chair cat-cow.

messages.From supported staff, bend knees and pla: From supported staff, bend knees and place feet flat before setting hands behind the hips.

messages.Identify IN and EX in the source table a: Identify IN and EX in the source table as inhalation and exhalation. Read the table on paper before attempting to coordinate movement.
messages.Identify kneeling frog and upright frog: Identify kneeling frog and upright frog variants by their leg and arm arrangements; names differ between traditions. Abdominal compression and deep knee flexion are reasons for individual teaching, not universal targets.
messages.Identify lotus as feet placed on opposit: Identify lotus as feet placed on opposite thighs; do not pull a foot into position or press a knee down. NCCIH advises beginners to avoid lotus.
messages.Identify where a familiar standing pathw: Identify where a familiar standing pathway ends and individual floor instruction begins.
messages.If a rear-foot return needs a hop, shoul: If a rear-foot return needs a hop, should you lengthen the stance or shorten it before a symptom-free retest?
messages.If choosing a small forward inclination,: If choosing a small forward inclination, you may rest arms on a second firm support over the legs; it must not draw the torso deeper. Keep the head in a comfortable neutral direction forward/down rather than hanging the neck. Stay only in a comfortable small shape without locking knees or pulling the legs. If no forward inclination is comfortable at setup, return to neutral and omit the shape.
messages.If choosing movement, use only the neces: If choosing movement, use only the necessary brief rehearsal in a familiar smaller form and never retry after symptoms. Keep knowledge, self-report and actual observation separate.
messages.If comfortable, bend the front knee only: If comfortable, bend the front knee only a little while torso stays upright; hands remain supported. No deep lunge, chest thrust or overhead arms are needed. Use ordinary breaths and stop before instability.
messages.If comfortable, lift one foot just clear: If comfortable, lift one foot just clear of the floor with the knee bent, keeping the other sole grounded and the trunk quiet. No target lift height is needed.
messages.If comfortable, turn the ribs a little l: If comfortable, turn the ribs a little left; let the head follow the torso, not turn farther. Keep the pelvis facing forward without forcing it rigid.
messages.If new health limits make the old plan u: If new health limits make the old plan uncertain, use observation and individual guidance instead of assuming an earlier adaptation still applies.
messages.If practising, follow the chosen ordinar: If practising, follow the chosen ordinary or short route at your own pace with neutral resets, ordinary breath and rest. Use exits and omissions when limits change; never chase the timer.
messages.If prone contact is appropriate, lower t: If prone contact is appropriate, lower through your side to the abdomen; place forearms parallel with elbows under or slightly ahead of shoulders.
messages.If ready, set an upper limit of about on: If ready, set an upper limit of about one minute and re-enter the same small shape. While waiting attend to support, ordinary breath or a fixed point around you.
messages.If stable, float the rear foot a little: If stable, float the rear foot a little with both hands supported; lengthen forward and back without demanding a horizontal Warrior III shape.
messages.If steady, rest the free foot against th: If steady, rest the free foot against the ankle or calf, never pressing into the knee joint.
messages.If support and small range cannot be arr: If support and small range cannot be arranged, select neutral back lying and do not call it a twist. Stay only up to the shared limit or leave earlier, head centred and breath ordinary. Bring knees gradually to centre, comfortably reset foot contact and pause in neutral.
messages.If that link is familiar and symptom-fre: If that link is familiar and symptom-free, include just one selected optional component. Return upright and pause before a foot changes position. Continuous attention includes stationary pauses; speed is not progression.
messages.If the hips stay far from the heels, add: If the hips stay far from the heels, add height under the chest instead of pressing down. Knee or ankle discomfort ends the shape; sitting upright or lying on the back is the replacement.
messages.If today’s setup is appropriate and the: If today’s setup is appropriate and the components familiar, rehearse the chosen short route; otherwise observe. Afterwards label each component practised/self-reported, observed, knowledge-only, omitted or unresolved.
messages.If you choose the supine route, lift one: If you choose the supine route, lift one bent knee only as comfortable, return that foot fully to the mat before switching sides, then reset both feet on the mat before a small bridge; lower fully and choose rest.
messages.If you need hand support, use a verified: If you need hand support, use a verified solid wall within easy reach. A door, glass panel, desk or moving chair is not a support for this route.
messages.If you only observe from a chair, how sh: If you only observe from a chair, how should the result be labelled?
messages.In a chair, turn the head a little each: In a chair, turn the head a little each way and roll shoulders slowly without tipping back.
messages.In a later separate session, before open: In a later separate session, before opening the page explain your adaptation of Yin waiting, two selected shapes, each support/entry/neutral/exit, a reason to leave before time and the different responses to symptoms versus symptom-free setup errors.

In a later separate session, before opening the plan, recall the setup, return points and two different responses: a symptom-free contact error and a stop symptom. Then compare the plan and correct gaps on paper before choosing movement.
messages.In a triangle variation, the lower hand: In a triangle variation, the lower hand can rest lightly on the seat of a chair while the feet are set apart.
messages.In neutral distinguish “time ended,” “at: In neutral distinguish “time ended,” “attention wandered,” “setup error” and “symptom”; several may apply. Never deliberately provoke symptoms.
messages.In our standing adaptations, use ordinar: In our standing adaptations, use ordinary unforced breathing. Pause and breathe freely between actions; do not lengthen or hold breath to keep up.
messages.In the traditional order, standing funda: In the traditional order, standing fundamentals follow Sun A and Sun B: forward folds holding the toes or with hands under the feet, Triangle and its revolved form, Side Angle and its revolved form, four wide-leg folds and an intense side stretch.

If movement has not been observed, record “self-report/not observed.” The next goal is resolving the identified uncertainty, not deeper or longer waiting. Unsupported, advanced or prolonged Yin remains outside this pathway.

messages.Individual range, non-forcing and leavin: Individual range, non-forcing and leaving only.
messages.Inhale and return through neutral into a: Inhale and return through neutral into a small opening; avoid throwing the head back.
messages.Initiate a small Vakrasana turn without: Initiate a small Vakrasana turn without using the arms as levers.
messages.Integrate Warriors, triangle and hinge b: Integrate Warriors, triangle and hinge balance using deliberate foot resets.

messages.It gives a distinct reset before changin: It gives a distinct reset before changing feet; do not pivot or turn a loaded stance to chase the next side.
messages.Keep a hand on the wall or practise seat: Keep a hand on the wall or practise seated foot contact if standing is uncomfortable.
messages.Keep a needed hand supported and arms lo: Keep a needed hand supported and arms low. The back heel may stay lifted in this adaptation; do not twist a loaded foot or force the traditional heel/hip position.
messages.Keep a stable wheelless rest chair avail: Keep a stable wheelless rest chair available if you already use it comfortably. Plan to return to ordinary standing or seated rest; no floor transfer is required.
messages.Keep a wall hand and arms low; choose mo: Keep a wall hand and arms low; choose mountain or the previously learned short lunge if this foot position is unsuitable.
messages.Keep arms low and folds tiny; use single: Keep arms low and folds tiny; use single familiar stations or study the map without movement.
messages.Keep arms low or raise the free arm only: Keep arms low or raise the free arm only within the range learned in a04. Breathe freely; staying in the position for a count is optional.
messages.Keep both arms low or keep one hand on t: Keep both arms low or keep one hand on the wall; observe instead if standing is unsuitable.
messages.Keep both feet grounded or observe when: Keep both feet grounded or observe when falling is a concern; a wall or chair cannot remove fall risk or establish pregnancy suitability.
messages.Keep both hands in front of the body, or: Keep both hands in front of the body, or omit the overhead arm.
messages.Keep both sitting bones down and lean le: Keep both sitting bones down and lean less. The reach is small by design; distance is not the goal.
messages.Keep both sitting bones supported and ma: Keep both sitting bones supported and make room to turn without hooking an arm around the chair.
messages.Keep deliberate arrival, return and rest: Keep deliberate arrival, return and rest while linking chosen actions.
messages.Keep feet fixed while learning a shallow: Keep feet fixed while learning a shallow supported wall preparation and its return.
messages.Keep hand contact, bring hips over the f: Keep hand contact, bring hips over the feet and return the trunk to upright together. Do not snap the knees straight or roll up from a deep dangling fold. If entry/return is unfamiliar, study h11 with an instructor instead of experimenting here.
messages.Keep hands in the lap and shorten the le: Keep hands in the lap and shorten the lesson if breath focus is uncomfortable.
messages.Keep knees pointing along the feet, coll: Keep knees pointing along the feet, collarbones broad and neck in line with the torso; maintain an easy breath instead of dropping the head back.
messages.Keep knees soft and gaze forward or slig: Keep knees soft and gaze forward or slightly up; breathe normally and avoid dropping the head or seeking a deep lower-back bend.
messages.Keep knees soft and leave by rolling ont: Keep knees soft and leave by rolling onto the side rather than sitting straight up.
messages.Keep one precise question for a trained: Keep one specific unresolved teaching question and return to its named lesson before deciding on another taught unit. Compare the written explanation first. Completion means participation records reached the end; it is not an observed assessment of practice.
messages.Keep only familiar basic shapes; optiona: Keep only familiar basic shapes; optional intermediate preparations are not a test.
messages.Keep shoulders easy. During any comforta: Keep shoulders easy. During any comfortable inhalation, let the free arm travel forward only as far as is easy, below shoulder height if preferred. Do not lift the chin to accompany it.
messages.Keep the angle described for this test;: Keep the angle described for this test; more than {degrees}° of turn and the reading is not used.
messages.Keep the base while returning one small: Keep the base while returning one small arm or foot action to support.
messages.Keep the closing rest and leave out a sh: Keep the closing rest and leave out a shape. A shorter practice that ends in rest follows the plan; rushing through every shape does not.
messages.Keep the front knee above or behind the: Keep the front knee above or behind the front ankle and slide the back knee back only a little on the padding. Hands rest on the blocks or on the front thigh; the trunk stays upright enough that breathing stays ordinary.
messages.Keep the knee bend small and the top han: Keep the knee bend small and the top hand on the hip; choose map study if the stance is uncertain.
messages.Keep the knees bent and use the chair se: Keep the knees bent and use the chair seat for the hands; map study replaces the fold whenever standing is uncertain.
messages.Keep the left foot grounded and take one: Keep the left foot grounded and take one short familiar step back with the right, preserving sideways width rather than a tightrope line. The back heel may be lifted; keep the front knee soft and tracking with its toes. Avoid twisting on a loaded foot.
messages.Keep the lesson closed. In the chosen su: Keep the lesson closed. In the chosen supported Butterfly version, what stays in place while the knees are still supported out to the sides? Explain the order for becoming upright, unloading the optional forearm bolster and returning the thighs toward centre. If that order is not familiar, what should the learner choose instead of improvising?
messages.Keep the lift very small or practise a s: Keep the lift very small or practise a seated pelvic tilt instead. Pregnancy may require avoiding prolonged flat-back lying; seek individual advice rather than treating this option as clearance.
messages.Keep the neck in line with the torso, ga: Keep the neck in line with the torso, gaze toward the floor ahead; do not crane the chin to look at the phone. Take ordinary breaths in the chosen shallow shape.
messages.Keep the neck long, breathe without abdo: Keep the neck long, breathe without abdominal strain and slide elbows farther forward to reduce the lift.
messages.Keep the other foot grounded and breathe: Keep the other foot grounded and breathe normally. The paired straight-leg Ardha Halasana is identified for instructor guidance, not assigned as an independent next step.
messages.Keep the reaching hand below shoulder he: Keep the reaching hand below shoulder height or sit in a chair.
messages.Keep the rear knee down and the front fo: Keep the rear knee down and the front foot flat; move the pelvis forward only a little while the front knee follows the toes.
messages.Keep the review entirely written and sto: Keep the review entirely written and stop when tired.
messages.Keep the step short and wall support; if: Keep the step short and wall support; if transfer is unfamiliar, choose written side identification instead.
messages.Keep the uncertainty visible. Name the t: Keep the uncertainty visible. Name the term or transition you cannot explain; reread that part or prepare a question for a suitable teacher. Do not turn an unknown into a technique correction.
messages.Keep the wall within easy reach and firs: Keep the wall within easy reach and first transfer weight with both toes still on the floor.
messages.Keep the written plan for h42, with a se: Keep the written plan for h42, with a separate note for each shape you have only observed.
messages.Keep this a written task. With the sourc: Keep this a written task. With the source closed, mark the right/left front-foot positions and the repeated floor group in the seventeen-count map. Reopen the table to correct one written position, then close it and recall that position again. No movement, jump or floor transition is required to check the answer.
messages.Keep toes on the floor or both hands on: Keep toes on the floor or both hands on a stable chair.
messages.Keeping both palms in contact and knees: Keeping both palms in contact with the wall and knees soft, move the hips a little back and incline the trunk only a little. Elbows may straighten comfortably, never lock. This limited high wall variation is a preparation related to Downward Dog, not its floor form; no horizontal torso or head-below-hips target.
messages.Kneel on a padded surface with a bolster: Kneel on a padded surface with a bolster or firm cushions lengthwise in front of you. A folded blanket can go under the ankles or between the thighs and calves.
messages.Kneel on padding only if comfortable and: Kneel on padding only if comfortable and place hands at the back of the pelvis.
messages.Knees apart, big toes together; seated k: Knees apart, big toes together; seated kneeling base.
messages.Knees-down lowering order, elbows near t: Knees-down lowering order, elbows near the body and the small cobra return to all fours.
Knowledge only. Do not copy these poses. Original stylized schematics show names and contact points, not anatomical measurements, personal suitability or safety approval. Entry, support and exit need qualified instruction.
messages.Knowledge-only comparison; remain seated: Knowledge-only comparison; remain seated or upright in the already comfortable position. No transfer is requested. Replace an unearned physical claim with “knowledge-only/unresolved” and explain the difference again in writing. Carry this boundary into v09. Optional future floor instruction expands the route only after separate demonstration and observation, never automatically.
messages.Language is saved on this installation a: Language is saved on this installation and does not change your account or practice records.
messages.Later recall and the next teaching quest: Later recall and the next teaching question
messages.Later recall plus a route choice and opt: Later recall plus a route choice and optional actual rehearsal. An instructor still needs to observe actual support, entry, transitions and exit to judge physical teaching adequacy. Re-explain a corrected memory gap unaided; a repeated movement attempt uses v08 and never tests a symptom.  A self-selected repeatable supported standing route; explainable breath/movement choices, contact and controlled returns; independent stop/modify decisions; later recall with honest omissions. Record each criterion separately as explained, self-reported or unresolved. All units read, a timer completed or an app tick is insufficient. Floor cycle, advanced inversion, named-tradition proficiency, teacher qualification and health outcomes are outside the endpoint.
messages.Lay out mountain, supported forward fold: Lay out mountain, supported forward fold, tabletop, small cobra and rest as separate stations.
messages.Lean the upper body only a little to the: Lean the upper body only a little to the left, keeping both sitting bones on the seat and the head in line with the trunk. Ordinary breathing continues; no hold at the end of the range.
messages.Learn a gentle Nadi Shodhana pattern wit: Learn a gentle Nadi Shodhana pattern without retaining breath.
messages.Learn a split stance and a controlled re: Learn a split stance and a controlled return to tabletop.
messages.Learn an open standing base without turn: Learn an open standing base without turning on a loaded knee.
messages.Learn small entries and returns before l: Learn small entries and returns before linking.
messages.Learn the hip-back action with two disti: Learn the hip-back action with two distinct support choices.
messages.Leave the position if head or eye pressu: Leave the position if head or eye pressure, dizziness, pain or unusual breathlessness appears.
messages.Leave this unattempted. Read the example: Leave this unattempted. Read the example before another written recall; elapsed time does not establish learning.
messages.Left and right measured separately on th: Left and right measured separately on those joints — never averaged into one figure, because a stiff left shoulder and a mobile right one are not one number
messages.Legs up a wall and legs on a chair are s: Legs up a wall and legs on a chair are separate supine rest setups.
messages.Lengthen the torso without pressing into: Lengthen the torso without pressing into the lower back; breathe normally and reduce the stride if abdomen or knee feels compressed.
messages.Lengthen the trunk a little and come par: Lengthen the trunk a little and come partway up for the halfway-lift station. Keep the neck easy; do not lift the chin to chase a gaze target.
messages.Lengthen through the crown as you breath: Lengthen through the crown as you breathe, then shake out the legs.
messages.Lengthen up, move the chest slightly for: Lengthen up, move the chest slightly forward and return upright before any back pinch.
messages.Lengthen upward first and lift the breas: Lengthen upward first and lift the breastbone a little; allow only a small upper-body extension without pushing the hips forward.
messages.Let arms and jaw relax; keep the breath: Let arms and jaw relax; keep the breath ordinary and leave slowly through the side.
messages.Let arms rest and lengthen through the c: Let arms rest and lengthen through the crown without pushing the ribs forward.
messages.Let breathing follow its ordinary rhythm: Let breathing follow its ordinary rhythm: no deepening, slowing, retention or matching seconds. The first entry/exit rehearsal is a brief trial, not a completed Yin hold. If setup is comfortable and the exit is known, you may choose to stay for up to about one minute; leaving earlier is always valid. In a later comfortable session you may choose up to two minutes; more time or depth is not a progression requirement. Do not deepen during the same hold in this introduction. A timer reminds you of an upper limit, not an endurance target. Eyes may remain open. When attention wanders, return to contact/ordinary breathing without pulling yourself into a model appearance. Familiar floor access is required, not taught by reading h35. Movement may be omitted; knowledge/self-report/observed movement stay separate. See y01/y02 for the complete setup and personal-limit conditions.
messages.Let one arm travel forward in a small ar: Let one arm travel forward in a small arc, palm inward, elbow soft. Stop below shoulder height or earlier where comfortable; do not reach overhead to prove a pose.
messages.Let the arms rest by the sides. Lift the: Let the arms rest by the sides. Lift the shoulders a little toward the ears, then lower them slowly; then draw them a little back and release. Head stays level.
messages.Let the head hang in line with the trunk: Let the head hang in line with the trunk, not lower. Stay for a few ordinary breaths; the traditional five-breath count is optional.
messages.Let the knees open as wide as is comfort: Let the knees open as wide as is comfortable and walk the hands forward to lower the chest onto the bolster. The forehead or one cheek rests on the bolster or on the hands.
messages.Let the pelvis face forward only as comf: Let the pelvis face forward only as comfortable; raise arms or keep hands on hips, with ribs over pelvis and an easy breath.
messages.Let the pelvis settle completely, rest w: Let the pelvis settle completely, rest with knees bent and use a side roll to leave.
messages.Let the upper back round a little and th: Let the upper back round a little and the chin come gently toward the chest, hands staying on the thighs. Move slowly; this is not a forward fold.
messages.Lie comfortably with both feet on the fl: Lie comfortably with both feet on the floor and bring one knee above the hip only as far as easy.
messages.Lie face down only if comfortable, with: Lie face down only if comfortable, with forearms folded and head turned gently to one side.
messages.Lie in a comfortable position with suppo: Lie in a comfortable position with support under knees, or choose side lying or a chair.
messages.Lie on your back only if comfortable; ke: Lie on your back only if comfortable; keep one foot on the floor and guide the other knee gently inward.
messages.Lie on your back, side-on to the camera,: Lie on your back, side-on to the camera, with both legs straight. Keeping the other leg flat on the floor, raise the leg nearest the camera as high as you can with the knee straight. Lower it slowly.
messages.Lie with feet on the floor and knees ben: Lie with feet on the floor and knees bent; keep arms relaxed beside the body.
messages.Lift and lower the pelvis with a control: Lift and lower the pelvis with a controlled range.
messages.Lift one bent knee toward the hip as in: Lift one bent knee toward the hip as in h27; optionally extend that lower leg toward the ceiling only as far as the back stays comfortable.
messages.Lift the chest a little from belly rest: Lift the chest a little from belly rest and return to tabletop or child shape.
messages.Lift the chest a little without pushing: Lift the chest a little without pushing through the lower back.
messages.Lift the head and upper chest only a lit: Lift the head and upper chest only a little, using the back body more than the arms. Keep the elbows bent and the neck long; there is no straight-arm upward dog in this lesson.
messages.Link each station with an ordinary breat: Link each station with an ordinary breath and pause between them. If one link is not familiar today, leave it out of the plan rather than testing it inside the flow.
messages.Link familiar blocks while preserving re: Link familiar blocks while preserving rest and safe ways to change floor orientation.
messages.Link shallow knee bend and separate righ: Link shallow knee bend and separate right/left steps using taught returns.
messages.Link the standing Sun A elements: Link the standing Sun A elements

messages.Load the arms gently before any Purvotta: Load the arms gently before any Purvottanasana variation.
messages.Locate Saral Matsyasana in the syllabus: Locate Saral Matsyasana in the syllabus while separating knowledge from unsupervised neck loading.
messages.Locate the raised chest, arm support and: Locate the raised chest, arm support and head position; notice that similar-looking versions place different loads on the neck.
messages.Look and turn a little to one side; come: Look and turn a little to one side; come back through centre before the other.
messages.Look around before resuming another task: Look around before resuming another task. Record what anchor you used and whether you shortened the rest, without claiming reduced pain, stress or improved health.
messages.Look around, move the fingers and remain: Look around, move the fingers and remain supported before choosing the next action. If watching breath feels uncomfortable, use the stationary object throughout.
messages.Lower arms, straighten the front knee so: Lower arms, straighten the front knee softly and use the wall to step back to mountain; reset before the other side.
messages.Lower chest and forehead first, release: Lower chest and forehead first, release the hands and use the side-roll exit before sitting.
messages.Lower knees, use the chair to reach a su: Lower knees, use the chair to reach a supported seat, then stand slowly into mountain. A standing-only wall sequence may end here without floor stations.
messages.Lower legs and chest under control, rele: Lower legs and chest under control, release the effort completely and leave through the h16 side-roll route.
messages.Lower the arm during an ordinary exhalat: Lower the arm during an ordinary exhalation if convenient. If the breath changes sooner, pause the arm or use another breath; there is no one-breath deadline.
messages.Lower the arm to the thigh and pause bef: Lower the arm to the thigh and pause before the other side. For the optional chest opening, start with both hands resting on the thighs. Bend both elbows gently and lift the hands just clear of the thighs, keeping them low beside the waist, palms facing inward. Move the bent elbows only a little sideways, without pushing the chest forward or tipping the head back. Return both hands to the thighs. This separate optional movement is not Fish pose.
messages.Lower the arms and stop for pain, dizzin: Lower the arms and stop for pain, dizziness or loss of balance. Do not repeat to test a symptom.
messages.Lower the arms slowly and return to ordi: Lower the arms slowly and return to ordinary standing. Pause with free breathing; end at your planned rest if needed.
messages.Lower the chest and forehead back to the: Lower the chest and forehead back to the mat and rest a moment. A lower back pinch or a neck strain ends the lift; rest on the belly or turn the head to one side.
messages.Lower the chest from tabletop with knees: Lower the chest from tabletop with knees down and return to tabletop without collapsing.
messages.Lower the chest, rest the forehead, rele: Lower the chest, rest the forehead, release forearms and leave through the side-roll taught in h16.
messages.Lower the foot gently before choosing th: Lower the foot gently before choosing the other side. If lifting encourages leaning or strain, keep both feet down and return to c03 toe work or rest.
messages.Lower the foot slowly and switch sides w: Lower the foot slowly and switch sides without arching to gain height.
messages.Lower the hand and breathe through both: Lower the hand and breathe through both nostrils; stop the exercise if air hunger or dizziness appears.
messages.Lower the lifted leg completely, release: Lower the lifted leg completely, release the toes and use the prone side-roll exit after the last repetition.
messages.Lower the phone to floor height for this: Lower the phone to floor height for this test.
messages.Lower the seat before lifting either han: Lower your pelvis back to sitting before lifting either hand, then rest your wrists without rolling onto them.
messages.Lower through the side onto the mat, wit: Lower through the side onto the mat, with both knees bent; choose seated observation if back lying is unsuitable.
messages.Lower to a padded kneeling seat using a: Lower to a padded kneeling seat using a stable support; place the hands before shifting weight forward.

messages.Make a correction decision without diagn: Make a correction decision without diagnosing yourself.

Compare smaller shoulder and ankle movements with the familiar range.
messages.Make only a written space/exit plan; lea: Make only a written space/exit plan; leave movement for another suitable session.
messages.Make smaller motions or omit a region th: Make smaller motions or omit a region that feels uncomfortable; seek individual advice for recent injury.
messages.Make the hinge very small, keep wall sup: Make the hinge very small, keep wall support or study the sequence without movement.
messages.Make three small lifts separated by comp:
Make three small lifts separated by complete seated rest.

Compare a small seated unweighting with observation before raising the hips.

messages.Mark every untaught station/transfer on: Mark every untaught station/transfer on your paper. A name, picture or this written answer is not permission to perform it.

messages.Move between a small rounded back and a: Move between a small rounded back and a tall seat with hands on the thighs.
messages.Move between tabletop, a bent-knee dog a: Move between tabletop, a bent-knee dog and a knee-down lunge with hand support.
messages.Move between the two shapes a few times: Move between the two shapes a few times with ordinary breathing, then rest upright or against the backrest.
messages.Move hips slightly back and forward to f: Move hips slightly back and forward to find a position where wrists and knees can rest.
messages.Move neck, shoulders, wrists and ankles: Move neck, shoulders, wrists and ankles within a comfortable range.
messages.Move slowly for six cycles, then rest on:
Move slowly for six cycles, then rest on a chair or mat.

Compare a small tabletop wave with a seated small wave.
messages.Move the chest forward enough to make on: Move the chest forward enough to make one comfortable line from head through hips to knees; do not let the waist sag.
messages.Move through tabletop, cat-cow, optional: Move through tabletop, cat-cow, optional child rest and low cobra.
messages.Move through the written route once at y: Move through the written route once at your own pace. Any station can become the end of the practice; go straight to your planned rest if attention, contact or breathing becomes uncertain.
messages.Must feet move toward the wall or both h: Must feet move toward the wall or both hands release before the torso returns upright?
messages.Must floor vinyasas or a traditional Sun: Must floor vinyasas or a traditional Sun A be added before the supported standing endpoint is valid?
messages.Must the palms meet overhead or feet pre: Must the palms meet overhead or feet press together?
messages.Name a04 standing, the shallow fold, par: Name a04 standing, the shallow fold, partial rise and upright return before optional movement. If you have returned comfortably and only forgot the order, correct it on paper, then optionally try one smaller already-taught sequence with needed support. Compare the distinction between partial rise and upright return. Uncertain return or any stop symptom ends movement; do not test it again. Explain the two stops without the page.
messages.Name one difference between your written: Name one difference between your written answer and the reference. Revise just that point, hide the reference and explain it again in the same example. This compares written answers, not physical ability.
messages.Name required support at each stage, opt: Name required support at each stage, optional actions omitted, a breath-mismatch response and a symptom-stop response. Record floor actions as knowledge-only unless independently taught and observed outside this proposal.
messages.Name the actions that are already famili: For the optional standing route, identify the already taught h01/h02 boundaries and ordinary breathing, h03 supported standing and h05 small joint preparation, or those same familiar components you already know. This planning card is not the preparation itself. If any entry or return is new or unclear today, study it first and keep this route written; a completion mark is not permission.
messages.Name the central rest point, then explor: Name the central rest point, then explore one small reach per side. If, without a stop signal, the mistake is lifting a hip off the seat, return upright, reduce the lean and try once more. Pinching or any stop signal ends the action without retest.
messages.Name the finishing sequence as map knowl: Name the finishing sequence as map knowledge and close a practice with rest.
messages.Name the observed issue precisely: conta: Name the observed issue precisely: contact lost, trunk rocking or a rushed return. Pain, pinching, dizziness, tingling or unusual breathlessness belong to stopping, not a coordination pass/fail.
messages.Name the previously learned shapes befor: Name the previously learned shapes before arranging the mat and chair; no new pose is required in this map.
messages.Name the standing fundamentals that foll: Name the standing fundamentals that follow the sun salutations without practising them.
messages.Name the three forms and write one perso:
Name the three forms and write one personal question for a teacher; no physical performance is required.

Compare the three knowledge diagrams and select a question for a teacher.
messages.Name your central rest point, then explo: Name your central rest point, then explore a small turn and return. If the symptom-free mistake is pulling with the hand, release it, reduce the range and retry once with hands resting. Pinching or any stop symptom ends the action without retest.

messages.No. Inversions and lotus forms stay map: No. Inversions and lotus forms stay map knowledge and need a trained teacher. The Lissom closing is a supported seat and rest.

messages.Notice breathing without controlling or: Notice breathing without controlling or holding it.

messages.Notice ordinary breathing briefly; do no: Notice ordinary breathing briefly; do not label the seat a yoga pose.
messages.Notice two or three ordinary breaths; do: Notice two or three ordinary breaths; do not make them larger, slower or deeper. There is no retention, nose-only rule or breath count to achieve.
messages.Notices for the open-source software inc: Notices for the open-source software included in this app.
messages.Observe or choose seated chest opening i: Observe or choose seated chest opening if hand loading is unsuitable. This bent-knee version does not establish the straight-leg Purvottanasana skill.

messages.Omit physical execution, mark the uncert: Omit physical execution, mark the uncertainty and ask for instruction and individual review. An earlier record does not solve today’s uncertainty.
messages.Omit prone, supine, hand-loading or bala: Omit prone, supine, hand-loading or balance blocks according to your personal limits; there is no universal pregnancy sequence in this lesson.
messages.On paper choose the c01 setup, c02 atten: On paper choose the c01 setup, c02 attention, c03 preparation, one c04 arm action, optional c05 turn and supported rest. Replace an unsuitable action with neutral attention.
messages.On paper list the actions you have actua: On paper list the actions you have actually practised, ones observed only and ones omitted. Reading about a movement is not evidence of performing it.
messages.On paper name the front foot and the upr: On paper name the front foot and the upright pause for each side. Optional movement uses only the familiar short step and return taught here. If back at the stable upright base with no stop signal, a forgotten side may be corrected on paper before one smaller familiar step-and-return. Compare the named foot and neutral pause; never turn a loaded foot to change sides. Uncertainty or a stop symptom ends movement.
messages.On paper, choose the standing A adaptati: On paper, choose the standing A adaptation from a09, the standing B adaptation from a11, or written map study. Name the option explicitly.
messages.On paper, counts 1–6 are Utkatasana, fol: On paper, counts 1–6 are Utkatasana, fold, halfway lift, Chaturanga, upward dog and downward dog. These are names in a traditional map, not a new physical assignment.
messages.On the thigh, the shin or a block, at a: On the thigh, the shin or a block, at a height that keeps the trunk long. Reaching the floor or the toe is the traditional form, not the goal here.
messages.Once the familiar upright base and comfo: Once the familiar upright base and comfortable wall contact are restored, pause, then lower one hand to the thigh, followed by the other only if support is no longer needed. No foot approach occurs within this variation. If you cannot maintain comfortable contact/return at this distance, choose a shallower range or omit; do not improvise a backward/forward walking transition.
messages.One bent knee raised; the other foot sta: One bent knee raised; the other foot stays grounded with its knee bent.
messages.One foot lifts, one foot supports: One foot lifts, one foot supports
messages.One option: y03 → bent-knee seated neutr: One option: y03 → bent-knee seated neutral → y04 → neutral → familiar rest. Another: y03 → neutral → familiar lying transfer → suitable side(s) of y05 → back-lying neutral → familiar final exit.
messages.One point to revisit or ask about: One point to revisit or ask about
messages.One selected-side entry and return, then: One selected-side entry and return, then decide whether the other side is appropriate. A stationary two-foot base with breath attention is the replacement. Exit using the already familiar support route. If symptom-free, start neutral with a shorter step and retry once; if an ordinary return remains unclear, omit and seek instruction. Add to v06 only after a controlled familiar return. Otherwise the hinge loop alone remains the standing route.
messages.One shallow entry and controlled upright: One shallow entry and controlled upright return; arm rise is omitted so only one new decision is studied. A symptom-free rushed return: stop upright, shorten the hinge and rehearse one slower supported return. Discomfort is a stop, not an alignment puzzle. v04 requires a familiar supported return; unresolved return means observation and instruction.
messages.Only for the optional floor route, start: Only for the optional floor route, start in h13 tabletop, tuck toes and lift hips with bent knees; heels need not touch and weight stays shared through both hands.
messages.Open Settings to turn camera access on f: Open Settings to turn camera access on for Lissom.
messages.Open and close the hands slowly a few ti: Open and close the hands slowly a few times, then make small comfortable circles with the wrists in both directions. No pulling of the fingers with the other hand.
messages.Open and close the hands, then circle ea: Open and close the hands, then circle each ankle with the foot lifted slightly.
messages.Open arms only as comfortable and keep t: Open arms only as comfortable and keep the torso upright between the feet; look ahead or over the front hand without neck strain.
messages.Open the eyes, move fingers and toes, th: Open the eyes, move fingers and toes, then rise through a side or supported seat at your own pace.
messages.Open the sources and compare one written: Open the sources and compare one written point at a time. Correct an omission on paper; do not test a physical position to settle a memory question.
messages.Open your h36 plan and label this as a f: Open your h36 plan and label this as a foundations rehearsal before the later standing and flow lessons.
messages.Optional floor extension: a knees-down l: Optional floor extension: a knees-down link
messages.Optional notes stay on this page and are: Optional notes stay on this page and are discarded when you leave. No recording, score, progress update or mastery approval is created.
messages.Optionally curl the toes under and lift: Optionally curl the toes under and lift the hips back into a dog shape with knees clearly bent, as in h46. Stay only for a few ordinary breaths, then lower the knees back to tabletop.
messages.Order the shapes so that each transfer i: Order the shapes so that each transfer is familiar: for example seated shapes first, then belly lying, then back lying. Place the closing rest last.
messages.Original breath-linked supported standin: Original breath-linked supported standing route. Selected entries, transitions and exits; floor branch is knowledge-only. No fixed traditional sequence, physical mastery, health outcome or complete Vinyasa-domain acceptance is claimed. Preparation and taught foundational references follow below. Minutes are flexible reading estimates, not practice doses.
messages.Original demonstration and actual learne: Original demonstration and actual learner feedback are missing. This written record is participation, not observed form, physical eligibility or mastery.
messages.Original instructor demonstration and ac: Original instructor demonstration and actual learner feedback are missing. Written source review does not certify physical movement.
messages.Outer-thigh cushions stay in place. Then: Outer-thigh cushions stay in place. Then, while upright, keep one hand supporting on the floor while the other supports its same-side outer thigh to bring that knee inward; then switch hand support and close the other side. Do not remove cushions while thighs load them. Return to neutral with feet in front; pause comfortably before rearranging props.
messages.Pad the knees and place a chair beside y: Pad the knees and place a chair beside you for entry; keep hips above knees instead of reaching for heels.
messages.Pause and lower one knee then the other: Pause and lower one knee then the other to tabletop using support. Choose h48 knees-down plank, return to tabletop, then deliberately lower through a side rest to prone only if appropriate.
messages.Pause at a chair between balance and fol: Pause at a chair between balance and fold; there is no required pace.
messages.Pause at your own comfortable depth, the: Pause at your own comfortable depth with both hands supported and breathe normally. Begin the return only in the next step; do not stand first and then try to approach the chair.
messages.Pause in neutral as needed; a second sha: Pause in neutral as needed; a second shape is never compulsory. No requirement to extend to two minutes or perform all three shapes.
messages.Pause or omit the action and breathe fre: Pause or omit the action and breathe freely. A count is not an instruction to force breathing; no breathing grade is produced.
messages.Pause, let breathing return to its own p: Pause, let breathing return to its own pace and choose an external object or foot contact. This is introductory awareness, not assessment of a formal breathing technique. Try recalling the choice in a later session.
messages.Pause, then use the left-forward a07 ver: Pause, then use the left-forward a07 version if suitable and return upright. No loaded pivot, downward dog to lunge transfer or low push-up is inserted.
messages.Pause/lower the arm or take another ordi: Pause/lower the arm or take another ordinary breath; smaller movement next time.
messages.Perform the same small chest opening in: Perform the same small chest opening in a chair or skip kneeling.
messages.Perform the same small spinal motion sea: Perform the same small spinal motion seated with hands on thighs.
messages.Perform three short enter-pause-exit cyc:
Perform three short enter-pause-exit cycles, resting fully between them.

Common mistake: Knees lift or the trunk sags before returning to tabletop. Correction: Keep both knees supported and return to tabletop before sagging.

Compare a short knees-down pause with an earlier tabletop hold.
messages.Place a folded blanket beneath shins or: Place a folded blanket beneath shins or between heels and buttocks; enter slowly with a wall nearby.
messages.Place a folded blanket beside the wall;: Place a folded blanket beside the wall; start with hips farther away so the knees can remain bent.
messages.Place a folded blanket under the knees a: Place a folded blanket under the knees and hands beneath comfortable shoulder reach.
messages.Place a stable chair beside the forward: Place a stable chair beside the forward leg; begin with a shorter stance than your maximum reach.
messages.Place a stable chair or two firm blocks: Place a stable chair or two firm blocks in front of you. Step the feet wide, parallel to each other, at a width where you feel steady. Hands rest on the hips.
messages.Place and return a foot with awareness r: Place and return a foot with awareness rather than jumping between poses.
messages.Place both feet down, open the hands and: Place both feet down, open the hands and pause before standing; do not combine every joint movement at once.
messages.Place chair and wall within reach and st: Place chair and wall within reach and start in mountain; choose a short stance for h44 Warrior I.
messages.Place each foot fully down before the ot: Place each foot fully down before the other moves; finish with both knees bent and roll to the side.
messages.Place feet hip width apart, soften knees: Place feet hip width apart, soften knees and let arms rest near the ribs.
messages.Place forearms on a chair or skip weight: Place forearms on a chair or skip weight bearing for sensitive wrists or knees.
messages.Place hands on a chair, bend knees and s: Place hands on a chair, bend knees and send hips back while keeping space in the abdomen.
messages.Place hands on the secured chair and pra: Place hands on the secured chair and practise one small hip hinge before considering the floor route.
messages.Place the blanket before sitting and kee: Place the blanket before sitting and keep a chair available if the floor is difficult to reach.
messages.Place the elbows on the blanket a little: Place the elbows on the blanket a little ahead of the shoulders and rest the forearms on the floor. The chest lifts only as far as the forearms carry it; let the shoulders hang without pushing up.
messages.Plan a practice that links up to four ta: Plan a practice that links up to four taught shapes with neutral pauses and ends in closing rest.
messages.Plan a selected seated practice with fam: Plan a selected seated practice with familiar actions, replacements, exits and explicit limits.
messages.Plan and optionally practise one complet: Plan and optionally practise one complete beginner flow from standing to floor links and a closing rest.
messages.Plan familiar access, neutral intervals: Plan familiar access, neutral intervals and final exit without treating reading as transfer ability.
messages.Plan one short exploration with pauses a: Plan one short exploration with pauses and a familiar stopping station. The lesson minutes are reading/practice estimates, not exercise targets.
messages.Plan preparation, the h57 standing seque: Plan preparation, the h57 standing sequence, an optional h49 or h58 block, seated breath and rest; allow about 25–35 minutes with shorter choices.
messages.Plan support, waiting and controlled exi: Plan support, waiting and controlled exit; omissions remain valid.
messages.Plan the space, support and stopping poi: Plan the space, support and stopping point before movement.
messages.Plan the support height before kneeling,: Plan the support height before kneeling, then optionally rehearse one brief entry and exit. Child's shape can also be the rest after y09. Pregnancy, recent eating or knee limits can make another rest the better choice. Record the support used.
messages.Plan, stop, revisit and state what remai: Plan, stop, revisit and state what remains open.
messages.Point to your support, an exit route and:
Point to your support, an exit route and a comfortable rest position before moving.

messages.Pose-by-pose coaching and reference scor: Pose-by-pose coaching and reference scoring are not available.
messages.Postpone movement or review in writing u: Postpone movement or review in writing until the setup fits. Omission is an honest route choice, not failure; it does not verify march competence. Qualified observation of actual entries/actions/exits and later learning retention remains needed. Written source review cannot supply physical acceptance, instructor certification or a health result.
messages.Practice is optional at each step; pain: Practice is optional at each step; pain is not a target and the camera does not judge safety.
messages.Practice remains self-recorded; it is no: Practice remains self-recorded; it is not a posture grade.
