messages.Practise 25-30 minutes at your own pace;:
Practise 25-30 minutes at your own pace; record which parts were practiced and changed.

Common mistake: A participation record is treated as retained movement skill. Correction: Show your route and its adaptations; completion alone is not retained ability.

Repeat after a break with one taught easier choice and explain it.
messages.Practise a small kneeling chest opening: Practise a small kneeling chest opening without dropping the head back.
messages.Practise one 12-minute circuit with your:
Practise one 12-minute circuit with your chosen exclusions and rests.

Common mistake: The sequence keeps prone work despite a personal restriction. Correction: Enter each floor orientation separately and keep the rest choice.

Use a chair-only version with the same preparation and rest order.
messages.Practise one 12-minute sequence without:
Practise one 12-minute sequence without trying to match a model's range.

Common mistake: Floor transitions are rushed to match the demonstration's range. Correction: Use a controlled side or seated reset instead of hurried floor changes.

Rehearse the same rest route with chair alternatives and name the omissions.
messages.Practise one entry and exit per side twi:
Practise one entry and exit per side twice, holding only two or three comfortable breaths.

Common mistake: The pelvis is forced to face forward while the heel or knee twists. Correction: Choose a short stance and let the pelvis face forward only as comfortable, without forcing it.

Compare a shorter and familiar Warrior I stance with the same heel support.
messages.Practise one flow block and up to two op:
Practise one flow block and up to two optional strength blocks with generous pauses.

Common mistake: Fatigue from flow carries into a hurried loaded floor transition. Correction: Finish and rest between flow and separately set strength blocks.

Choose a flow-only or chair route with the same planned rest opportunities.
messages.Practise the h27-based one-leg option or:
Practise the h27-based one-leg option or explain the diagram; record practice and knowledge separately.

Common mistake: A one-leg preparation is recorded as full half-plough or shoulder stand. Correction: Keep one-leg preparation separate from paired-leg or shoulder-bearing shapes.

Compare the h27-based action with a labeled knowledge diagram, without copying the diagram physically.
messages.Practise the plan at your own pace withi: Practise the plan at your own pace within the shared time limits. Leaving a shape early or skipping one keeps the plan valid; do not lengthen holds to make up time.
messages.Practise the rise and the stepping in be: Practise the rise and the stepping in before the fold. Optionally one fold with the chair. If you came up too fast and there is no stop signal, pause, then plan a slower rise. The four traditional hand variations stay map knowledge.
messages.Practise three slow rounds with a pause:
Practise three slow rounds with a pause after each return.

Common mistake: A support change is rushed and interrupts ordinary breathing. Correction: Stop at each support change before moving to the next station.

Compare separate stations with a gently linked route while preserving pauses.
messages.Pregnancy advice cautions against exerci: Pregnancy advice cautions against exercise lying flat on the back for more than a few minutes, especially after 16 weeks.
messages.Pregnancy exercise guidance gives a sepa: Pregnancy exercise guidance gives a separate reason to discuss personal limits and avoid lying flat on the back as much as possible.
messages.Pregnancy or abdominal-contact restricti: Pregnancy or abdominal-contact restrictions call for omitting this prone block and seeking personal guidance; h40 is also prone, not an automatic safe substitute. Prone abdominal contact is not a general pregnancy option; observe when personal suitability is uncertain.
messages.Pregnancy, injury and chronic conditions: Pregnancy, injury and chronic conditions need individual advice about personal limits; gentle, chair or supported does not automatically mean suitable. Observing is a valid choice.
messages.Pregnancy, knee or hip concerns can chan: Pregnancy, knee or hip concerns can change suitability; this knowledge lesson gives no clearance for lotus, compression or kneeling.
messages.Prepare a folded blanket for the elbows: Prepare a folded blanket for the elbows and a cushion within reach before lying down. Come to belly lying by your familiar route; legs rest long and about hip-width apart.
messages.Prepare a standing route and an exit: Prepare a standing route and an exit
messages.Prepare as in c01/c03: a stable chair wi: Prepare as in c01/c03: a stable chair without wheels, feet flat and hip-width, sitting a little forward from the backrest.
messages.Prepare as planned in a03, then start in: Prepare as planned in a03, then start in the two-foot stance of a04. This is Lissom’s standing adaptation; the floor stations of traditional Sun A are omitted.
messages.Prepare c01/c03, face forward with soles: Prepare c01/c03, face forward with soles grounded and hands resting on thighs. Do not grip the chair to pull.
messages.Prepare one region at a time: Prepare one region at a time
messages.Prepare the chair again today. Follow on: Prepare the chair again today. Follow one station at a time, returning hands and feet to support before moving to the next; put the phone aside during movement.
messages.Prepare the side distinction of Warrior: Prepare the side distinction of Warrior A with a short standing adaptation.
messages.Prepare today’s support, review the c11: Prepare today’s support, review the c11 plan and choose physical practice, written review or observation honestly. Previous records never replace today’s preparation.
messages.Press forearms lightly and let the breas: Press forearms lightly and let the breastbone travel forward and up while the pelvis remains resting.
messages.Press gently through hands, lift the hea: Press gently through hands, lift the head with the torso and return to tabletop before sitting.
messages.Press into the feet to rise, lower the a: Press into the feet to rise, lower the arms, then turn the feet forward before changing sides.
messages.Press lightly into hands and feet, lift: Press lightly into hands and feet, lift the pelvis a little, and lower without neck strain.
messages.Press the floor lightly away so the shou: Press the floor lightly away so the shoulders do not sink toward the ears. Keep the knees down throughout; there is no push-up or plank in this lesson.
messages.Press through hands and feet to raise th: Press through hands and feet to raise the pelvis as far as the shoulders permit; move toward a table shape without forcing a level line.
messages.Press through the feet to straighten com: Press through the feet to straighten comfortably and return to ordinary standing. Rest before changing direction or repeating.
messages.Press through the feet, lift the pelvis: Press through the feet, lift the pelvis a little, then lower one part at a time.
messages.Preview only · practise the earlier less: Preview only · practise the earlier lesson first
messages.Preview: goal, understanding questions a: Preview: goal, understanding questions and sources. Physical steps and practice recording stay closed; practise prerequisites and prepare before movement.
messages.Progress from h40 single-leg work to an: Progress from h40 single-leg work to an optional small whole-body lift.
messages.Put both hands on the thighs and return: Put both hands on your thighs. If focusing on breathing becomes tiring, stop watching it and let breathing continue naturally.
messages.Put the phone {min}–{max} cm off the flo: Put the phone {min}–{max} cm off the floor.
messages.Raise the arms only to a comfortable hei: Raise the arms only to a comfortable height. Tilt the pelvis first, then lean the trunk to the right and rest the right hand on the thigh, shin or a block. Holding the big toe is not required.
messages.Raise the chair support or perform a sea: Raise the chair support or perform a seated hip hinge.
messages.Raise the chest a little using the upper: Raise the chest a little using the upper back; lower with control before the breath strains.
messages.Raise the free arm or both arms only as: Raise the free arm or both arms only as far as comfortable, keeping both feet grounded and gaze easy. Here the upward-arm station is not a one-leg tree balance.
messages.Raise the free arm or both arms within t: Raise the free arm or both arms within the a04 range, then lower and hinge shallowly as in a05. Keep needed support and breathe freely between actions.
messages.Raise the hands onto blocks or a chair,: Raise the hands onto blocks or a chair, take smaller steps, or stay in tabletop. Do not swing or jump the foot forward, and do not lift the back knee to make it fit.
messages.Raised chest and arched neck distinguish: Raised chest and arched neck distinguish this floor shape.
messages.Reach one arm up and a little to the sid: Reach one arm up and a little to the side and return through centre without leaning on the chair.
messages.Reach one leg long along the floor, lift: Reach one leg long along the floor, lift it slightly, lower, then switch.
messages.Reach over the front leg, rest the lower: Reach over the front leg, rest the lower hand on a chair and rise back with control.
messages.Reach the chest gently forward from hips: Reach the chest gently forward from hips and return upright before the breath tightens.
messages.Reach the toes back and breastbone forwa: Reach the toes back and breastbone forward; first lift only the chest a little, then lower before deciding whether to include legs.
messages.Reach upward first, then a little sidewa: Reach upward first, then a little sideways; return to centre before changing sides.
messages.Read Sun B and its two sides: Read Sun B and its two sides
messages.Read counts 1–3 as upward arms, forward: Read counts 1–3 as upward arms, forward fold and halfway lift. Start and return standing frame the counted sequence.
messages.Read only or postpone movement until a s: Read only or postpone movement until a stable fitted base exists. A seated adaptation cannot certify medical suitability or competence in another yoga tradition. Review chair stability and foot contact if missed, then explain again without the page.
messages.Read the finishing map seated: shoulder: Read the finishing map seated: shoulder stand, plough and related forms, fish, headstand, lotus forms, the lifted lotus and final rest. Apart from the final rest, none of these is taught in Lissom.
messages.Read the h41 plan and select a shorter f: Read the h41 plan and select a shorter foundation route if supports or energy have changed today.
messages.Read the h59 plan, prepare supports and: Read the h59 plan, prepare supports and confirm today's chosen blocks; mark observation or omission before starting when needed.
messages.Read the map once, close it and name the: Read the map once, close it and name the four Lissom adaptations and two traditional poses that remain map-only. Correct omissions on paper. No posture is demonstrated to answer a memory question.
messages.Read the order first, then optionally re: Read the order first, then optionally rehearse one small lowering and return. Wrist, shoulder or knee discomfort ends the attempt; choose belly rest or written study instead. If you only forgot to keep the elbows near the sides and there is no stop signal, return to tabletop, choose less range and try once more. Record the chosen range and return.
messages.Read the scenario first: a call interrup: Read the scenario first: a call interrupts c07 and the chair is moved while you are away. Decide on paper how to restart; do not move an occupied chair for the exercise.
messages.Read the setup and exit, then optionally: Read the setup and exit, then optionally one brief side at a time. If the front foot landed too close and there is no stop signal, return to tabletop and place it again. Deeper variations such as lifting the back knee or lowering onto the forearms are not part of this pathway.

Read the setup and exit, then optionally rehearse one brief entry and exit. If the elbows were placed too far back and there is no stop signal, lower the chest, move them forward and try once. Record the chosen height and whether you stayed or left early.
messages.Read the shared entry and stop rules. Pu: Read the shared entry and stop rules. Put your chosen wall and rest chair on a paper map; do not start a movement while reading the phone.
messages.Read the standing fundamentals map, use: Read the standing fundamentals map, use four clearly labelled standing adaptations and close with rest.
messages.Read the station names seated; skip phys: Read the station names seated; skip physical rehearsal entirely.
messages.Read the terms without moving or changin: Read the terms without moving or changing your breath.
messages.Read the traditional Sun A map: Read the traditional Sun A map
messages.Read the two written plans aloud and ide: Read the two written plans aloud and identify where you would stop after an interruption. Correction: if an exit or replacement is missing, add a previously taught neutral pause or rest, then recheck the paper plan without movement.
messages.Readable course cards showing taught IDs: Readable course cards showing taught IDs, duration choices and exits; separate practice, adapted practice and knowledge-only labels.
messages.Reading and written recall only; no move: Reading and written recall only; no movement is needed. Demonstration, personal suitability and physical technique require separate review.
messages.Reading h35 does not teach the unfamilia: Reading h35 does not teach the unfamiliar transfer. Leave y05 unresolved and choose only an already accessible taught seated option, chair knowledge/observation or postponement. Arrange supports outside the shape and move them only when unloaded. The paper plan cannot establish transfer ability or personal suitability.
messages.Reading this card is not a warm-up. Stop: Reading this card is not a warm-up. Stop for pain, dizziness or feeling unwell. This is your report, not a camera or medical check.
messages.Rear three-quarter Gomukhasana arms with: Rear three-quarter Gomukhasana arms with strap gap visible; front-hand alternative.
messages.Reassess today's conditions; a previous: Reassess today's conditions; a previous comfortable practice is not today's clearance.
messages.Recall setup, attention, preparation, se: Recall setup, attention, preparation, selected actions with neutral pauses and rest. Return attention to support/contact. A record describes participation in the chosen route, not physical mastery or medical suitability.
messages.Recall the plan in a later separate sess: Recall the plan in a later separate session and repair an omission without a mastery claim.
messages.Recheck stability, foot fit, space and p: Recheck stability, foot fit, space and personal limits, then renew preparation. Shorten, omit or observe; do not hurry or hold breath to finish. Recalling the old plan does not certify the changed setup.
messages.Reclining turn components, prop choices: Reclining turn components, prop choices and slow return only.
messages.Recognize Padmasana, Mandukasana and Utt: Recognize Padmasana, Mandukasana and Uttana Mandukasana without making them required achievements.
messages.Recognize the nine counted movements wit: Recognize the nine counted movements without attempting untaught floor stations.
messages.Recognize what a phone course can guide: Recognize what a phone course can guide and when to stop.
messages.Record this as a foundation checkpoint;: Record this as a foundation checkpoint; review unfamiliar transitions before starting the new h43–h60 skills.
messages.Reduce range or choose only head-and-eye: Reduce range or choose only head-and-eye turning if spinal rotation is uncomfortable.
messages.Reduce the knee bend, bring the rear foo: Reduce the knee bend, bring the rear foot forward with support, restore the two-foot neutral base and pause. Repeat on the other side only if familiar; do not change sides by pivoting loaded knees.
messages.Reduce the lift or do a seated march; no: Reduce the lift or do a seated march; no straight-leg lift is required. Pregnancy may require avoiding prolonged flat-back lying; seek individual advice rather than treating this option as clearance.
messages.Reference ranges vary by age. Choose you: Reference ranges vary by age. Choose your age range to continue so Lissom can use the appropriate range.
messages.Rehearse both entry and return before li: Rehearse both entry and return before linking transitions.
messages.Rehearse one round as separate stations,:
Rehearse one round as separate stations, then repeat only if entries and exits remain controlled.

Common mistake: Stations are linked before their entries and exits are understood. Correction: Treat Sun A as separate taught stations with chosen replacements.

Compare a chair route with a floor route only for stations already practised.
messages.Rehearse only the unfamiliar transitions: Rehearse once only a transition taught in an earlier lesson whose entry, support and exit you know and have used comfortably. Do not physically test a first-time or unresolved transition: keep it on paper, replace it with a familiar taught route or observation, then revise the plan before h60.
messages.Rehearse optional preparations and revie: Rehearse optional preparations and review foundations before new standing and flow skills.
messages.Rehearse the exit before the entry. Opti: Rehearse the exit before the entry. Optionally practise one side with a small knee bend. If the knee moved past the toes and there is no stop signal, straighten, shorten the stance and try once. Knee pain or a shoulder pinch ends the attempt.
messages.Rehearse the foot setup separately, then:
Rehearse the foot setup separately, then try two short holds per side.

Common mistake: The learner pivots on the loaded bent knee. Correction: Reset the feet before bending the front knee or changing direction.

Compare shallow Warrior II with a wider arm reach only when the base stays steady.
messages.Rehearse the hinge-to-upright link first: Rehearse the hinge-to-upright link first, without the optional steps. Notice a comfortable exhalation while entering and an inhalation while returning if they happen naturally; otherwise use several ordinary breaths.
messages.Rehearse the order once in writing, then: Rehearse the order once in writing, then optionally one small lift and lowering. Compare the height you chose with the height you could return from without effort. A larger arch is not progress. Stop signals end the attempt without a retest; a forgotten hand position without a stop signal can be corrected from belly rest.
messages.Rehearse the order twice without holding:
Rehearse the order twice without holding poses or adding speed.

Common mistake: An unfamiliar floor station is added from a complete flow video. Correction: Name the stations and exits before linking a sun-salutation route.

Map standing and chair routes without adding an untaught floor station.
messages.Rehearse the pause and reset without add: Rehearse the pause and reset without adding an unsafe prop. A missed reset is corrected by returning to c01 and doing one familiar small action only after setup, with its exit planned. Retest asks whether the new context was checked, not whether the original schedule was recovered.
messages.Rehearse the rise first: hands to hips,: Rehearse the rise first: hands to hips, knees bent, slow return. Then optionally one fold to a familiar depth. If you came up with straight legs and no stop signal occurred, plan bent knees for the next rise. Dizziness ends the attempt; sit down and rest.
messages.Rehearse the selected short route once a: Rehearse the selected short route once at your own pace. Write what was practised, observed, omitted or unresolved. Phone reading and movement are separate phases. If you merely forgot which foot to move and have no symptoms, reset upright and simplify to the hinge link once; do not add a new pose during correction. Explain a coherent start, breath choice and end from memory before independent planning. This self-report does not verify physical execution.
messages.Rehearse the side-roll entry first and d: Rehearse the side-roll entry first and decide whether the supine section belongs in today's plan.
messages.Rehearse two small extensions with a com:
Rehearse two small extensions with a complete mountain reset between them.

Common mistake: A small extension becomes a lumbar pinch or loss of balance. Correction: Lift the chest slightly while keeping the support base and a long neck.

Compare neutral mountain with a small extension without increasing the lean.
messages.Relax the jaw and lips without clenching: Relax the jaw and lips without clenching; keep the ears uncovered and shoulders down.
messages.Release hands and return to a neutral se: Release hands and return to a neutral seat; seek individual instruction before trying a floor fish variation or head contact.
messages.Release the leg slowly and compare sides: Release the leg slowly and compare sides without pulling the knee against the chest.
messages.Release the lower hand first, then lower: Release the lower hand first, then lower the raised arm slowly; shake out hands before swapping.
messages.Release the sound, take an ordinary brea: Release the sound, take an ordinary breath and wait before repeating; do not lengthen the hum competitively.
messages.Release the stance with a small supporte: Release the stance with a small supported step, then sit if needed.
messages.Remain in the same small shape within th: Remain in the same small shape within the shared limit without controlling breath. To exit return hands beside the hips, share load into them and gradually bring the torso upright. Do not pull the support out immediately. First bend one knee a little more and slide that foot closer, then the other, unloading the support.
messages.Reopen Lissom and check your records aga: Reopen Lissom and check your records again.
messages.Repeat the separate sequence on the othe: Repeat the separate sequence on the other side, then sit and release the effort; no pivot is made on a deeply bent loaded knee.
messages.Repeat three alternating turns without s:
Repeat three alternating turns without swinging the arms for momentum.

Common mistake: Arm swing supplies momentum for the turn. Correction: Turn gently from a stable base; let the feet reset when needed.

Compare a smaller and familiar standing turn with the same comfortable foot placement.
messages.Replace the rear toes first, bring torso: Replace the rear toes first, bring torso upright and step feet together before changing sides.
messages.Reported without any reference range — t: Reported without any reference range — the number is a reading, not a verdict.
messages.Reposition support while unloaded before: Reposition support while unloaded before choosing the left side under the same rules. The left may need a different small range/time or omission; never force symmetry. Finish with both knees central and feet on the floor, pause, and rise only through your familiar side-lying/supported-seat route. This modified feet-on-floor form differs from the source's knees-to-chest full twist and cannot grant permission for that version.
messages.Respond to changed space or support by r: Respond to changed space or support by rechecking rather than continuing from memory.
messages.Rest an elbow on support if needed and l: Rest an elbow on support if needed and leave both nostrils open while finding an ordinary breath.
messages.Rest briefly; compare with legs on a cha:
Rest briefly; compare with legs on a chair only if supine rest suits your personal limits, or choose side-lying or seated rest.

Common mistake with wall support: Trying to make this supported inversion more demanding, or holding a supine position beyond personal limits. Correction: With wall support, keep the knees relaxed and place the hips at a comfortable distance from the wall.

Compare legs on a chair with wall support; omit flat-back rest when personally restricted.
messages.Rest for one minute, then compare with s:
Rest for one minute, then compare with side lying or a supported chair.

Common mistake: Prone rest is retained despite neck or abdominal pressure. Correction: Rest without compressing the abdomen or rotating the neck to an extreme.

Compare prone observation with side-lying or chair rest according to personal limits.
messages.Rest for three minutes and notice whethe:
Rest for three minutes and notice whether a different support would help.

Common mistake: Stillness is prioritised over a needed change of rest position. Correction: Change the rest position whenever comfort or breathing changes.

Compare chair rest and an individually suitable lying rest without a stillness target.
messages.Rest forehead on stacked hands or a cush: Rest forehead on stacked hands or a cushion and return through tabletop slowly.
messages.Rest hands on thighs and let the shoulde: Rest hands on thighs and let the shoulders settle while breathing normally.
messages.Rest hands on thighs for two breaths, th: Rest hands on thighs for two breaths, then lift through hands and change to the chair.
messages.Rest on the forearms from belly lying an: Rest on the forearms from belly lying and leave by lowering the chest first.
messages.Rest prone only if comfortable with fore: Rest prone only if comfortable with forehead supported and arms by the sides.
Rest the left hand on the seat or thigh. Raise the right arm forward and up only as high as the shoulder is comfortable.
messages.Restart attention and a small familiar p: Restart attention and a small familiar preparation, then choose a shorter route or stop. Lost time does not require faster movement or skipping rest.
messages.Return and stop for joint pain, dizzines: Return and stop for joint pain, dizziness or balance loss; do not increase depth to satisfy a picture.
messages.Return both feet to the mat, roll to the: Return both feet to the mat, roll to the side and pause before sitting up.
messages.Return both hands to the thighs and use: Return both hands to the thighs and use the backrest. Continue ordinary breathing; no end-range hold or perfectly equal arm height is required.
messages.Return by pressing back up to tabletop,: Return by pressing back up to tabletop, or lower the whole front body to the mat and rest. Breathe in an ordinary way and pause in tabletop before any repeat.
messages.Return slowly to centre and pause. Try t: Return slowly to centre and pause. Try the right separately; ranges can differ. Ordinary breathing continues and no end-range hold is required.
messages.Return the chest above the pelvis, lower: Return the chest above the pelvis, lower hands and pause in mountain before walking.
messages.Return the chest over the pelvis, take s: Return the chest over the pelvis, take support and come to a chair or comfortable kneeling rest.
messages.Return the hand beside the thigh and set: Return the hand beside the thigh and settle upright. Use the chair for rest if already familiar; skip the arm action and observe breath if unsuitable.
messages.Return the raised foot to the floor befo: Return the raised foot to the floor before letting go of the wall; reset both feet for the other side.
messages.Return the right foot back to tabletop i: Return the right foot back to tabletop in small steps, pause, then use the left side under the same rules. Sides may differ; omitting one side is valid. End in tabletop or your familiar rest.
messages.Return through a small knee bend and slo: Return through a small knee bend and slowly come upright with weight through the feet. Pause before deciding whether to repeat.
messages.Return through a stable seat before stan: Return through a stable seat before standing again; there is no fixed breath count.
messages.Return through neutral and let the chest: Return through neutral and let the chest lift a little as the shoulders widen, eyes looking ahead, not up. Keep the lower back comfortable and avoid squeezing it.
messages.Return to a neutral seat after each shap: Return to a neutral seat after each shape and change sides deliberately.
messages.Return to mountain again, then choose h5: Return to mountain again, then choose h50 supported hinge balance or toe-down hinge; keep the same support plan on both sides and breathe normally.
messages.Return to mountain before setting h45 Wa: Return to mountain before setting h45 Warrior II. Straighten, lower arms and reset the feet before entering h09 supported triangle.
messages.Return to mountain or a chair after the: Return to mountain or a chair after the last station and mark where you would need extra instruction for a continuous flow.
messages.Return to mountain or sit; list which tr: Return to mountain or sit; list which transitions needed support instead of judging the depth of poses.
messages.Return to neutral upright standing and p: Return to neutral upright standing and pause. The adaptation separates the sides instead of reproducing the traditional floor transfers.
messages.Return to the chair or mat for quiet bre: Return to the chair or mat for quiet breathing; record effort, not a pose grade.
messages.Return to upright, lower the arm and pau: Return to upright, lower the arm and pause. Use the other side separately; ranges can differ and either side may be omitted.
messages.Review a03: clear nonslip standing space: Review a03: clear nonslip standing space, a verified solid wall for needed hand support and a familiar rest/exit. No floor transfer is required.
messages.Review h27 first. If back lying is suita: Review h27 first. If back lying is suitable, enter through the side with knees bent and both feet down; otherwise use the lesson diagram from a chair.
messages.Review h42 and list skills now practised: Review h42 and list skills now practised independently, skills needing support, and forms only studied as knowledge.
messages.Review the actual selected route, contro: Review the actual selected route, controlled returns and retained decisions without claiming mastery.
messages.Review the beginner map without claiming: Review the beginner map without claiming full-series or physical acceptance.
messages.Review the comfortable range and support: Review the comfortable range and support used in the previous lessons.
messages.Review y01/y02 setup and real Hatha foun: Review y01/y02 setup and real Hatha foundations. Floor access must already be familiar and comfortable; reading h35 or ticking this card does not establish transfer ability or suitability.
messages.Right foot forward at count 7, left foot: Right foot forward at count 7, left foot forward at count 11. Remembering that order is not physical performance evidence.
messages.Rotation happens in the plane the camera: Rotation happens in the plane the camera is looking down, so a single lens cannot recover it. We would rather leave the test out of the battery than print a number we cannot stand behind.
messages.Rotation of the hip or shoulder (a singl: Rotation of the hip or shoulder (a single camera cannot recover transverse-plane twist)
messages.Run one 12-minute sequence, note which s:
Run one 12-minute sequence, note which support helped and repeat on another day.

Common mistake: Foot direction changes occur without an upright reset. Correction: Reset upright between the five standing shapes.

Choose one shorter round with wall support and omit an uncertain balance.
messages.Samasthiti names the upright return poin: Samasthiti names the upright return point. Notice both feet on the ground without trying to freeze or force symmetry.
messages.Samasthiti names upright standing and th: Samasthiti names upright standing and the return point of Sun A.
messages.Saving is taking longer than expected. Y: Saving is taking longer than expected. Your previous appearance is still active. You can close this dialog.
messages.Seated arm/ankle/march/turn components a: Seated arm/ankle/march/turn components and stopping for sudden illness; author chooses smaller rehearsal ranges.
messages.Seated close view with tiny sound wavefo: Seated close view with tiny sound waveform only; visibly return to ordinary breathing.
messages.Seated close-ups of four regions, one at: Seated close-ups of four regions, one at a time, with small-range and rest alternatives.
messages.Seated movement with a steady base: Seated movement with a steady base
messages.Seated rounding and lengthening of the s: Seated rounding and lengthening of the spine
messages.Secure the chair against a wall and stan: Secure the chair against a wall and stand far enough away to place both palms without leaning on a moving seat.
messages.Select chair, side lying or back lying b: Select chair, side lying or back lying before settling; support the head and knees as needed without covering the face.
messages.Select one taught shape already chosen c: Select one taught shape already chosen comfortably. Describe support and exit; first rehearse a brief entry/exit.
messages.Select suitable standing, seated and opt: Select suitable standing, seated and optional intermediate elements.
messages.Selected concept or component only; see: Selected concept or component only; see source map.
messages.Self-occlusion: lying on the floor hides: Self-occlusion: lying on the floor hides most landmarks from a side camera
messages.Send hips back while lengthening the sid: Send hips back while lengthening the sides of the torso; stop before shoulders or breath feel compressed.
messages.Separate Ashtanga foundations from a com: Separate Ashtanga foundations from a complete Primary Series.
messages.Separate breath attention from breath co: Separate breath attention from breath control.
messages.Separate labeled knowledge diagram from: Separate labeled knowledge diagram from seated demonstration; no head-bearing transition animation or visual claim of equivalence.
messages.Separate the traditional Sun A/B maps fr: Separate the traditional Sun A/B maps from Lissom’s two standing adaptations. The full Primary Series, floor transfers and finishing instruction are outside this beginner course.
messages.Separately, keep one heel grounded and l: Separately, keep one heel grounded and lift its toes a little; lower the toes. Try the other side only after the first foot rests flat. Do not lift the leg to enlarge the motion.
messages.Set a chair or cushion nearby before cho: Set a chair or cushion nearby before choosing which floor movements to include.
messages.Set a low forehead support and choose si: Set a low forehead support and choose side or chair observation when abdomen contact is unsuitable.
messages.Set feet roughly hip width with heels wi: Set feet roughly hip width with heels within easy reach; keep the back of the head resting and do not turn it during a lift.
messages.Set supports first; use the breath to sl: Set supports first; use the breath to slow transitions, not to force their timing.
messages.Set up a comfortable space and practice: Set up a comfortable space and practice without forcing a shape.
messages.Set up c01 and use c03 gently first. Onl: Set up c01 and use c03 gently first. Only if comfortable, move your sitting position a little toward the front of the seat, keeping both sitting bones supported. This means moving on the seat, not leaning the torso forward. Keep the head above the trunk; no chin lift is required.
messages.Set up each chosen floor orientation fro: Set up each chosen floor orientation from a neutral side or seated position, complete one short attempt and release fully before the next block.
messages.Set up hands and knees without treating: Set up hands and knees without treating one alignment as universal.
messages.Set up side-on to the camera in a forear: Set up side-on to the camera in a forearm plank, body in one straight line from head to heels. Hold as steady as you can for up to 45 seconds. Come down when your form breaks or you need to stop.

messages.Share pressure across the palms and brea: Share pressure across the palms and breathe normally for a short pause; stop sooner if shoulders collapse or breathing becomes effortful.
messages.Shift back, place both hands on support: Shift back, place both hands on support and return the front knee beside the rear knee before changing sides.
messages.Shift hips back toward tabletop before t: Shift hips back toward tabletop before taking weight off the hands; this lesson does not ask for a low push-up or full Chaturanga.
messages.Shift hips toward heels only as comforta: Shift hips toward heels only as comfortable, remove weight from hands and come to a supported seat.
messages.Shorten stance, keep hands on hips or us: Shorten stance, keep hands on hips or use a wall hand; observation is available when standing balance is uncertain.

messages.Side and three-quarter continuous lift a: Side and three-quarter continuous lift and lowering; label chest-only, the h40 single-leg recap and optional combined lift, keeping neck and pelvis visible.
messages.Side and three-quarter views, padded rea: Side and three-quarter views, padded rear knee and flat front foot close-up; show hand repositioning and return in real time.
messages.Side close view of low Bhujangasana, sma: Side close view of low Bhujangasana, small chest lift and controlled return; show skip branch.
messages.Side close-up of chest rising before a s: Side close-up of chest rising before a small arc; show return to vertical, wall hand and neutral-neck alternative. Label preparation, not a required deep backbend.
messages.Side close-up of forearms and pelvis con: Side close-up of forearms and pelvis contact; include a smaller lift, normal-speed lowering and clearly separate chair observation.
messages.Side entry and full lowering, wrist plac: Side entry and full lowering, wrist placement close-up and small-height comparison; show no head drop or unsupported straight-leg progression.
messages.Side full-body Setubandhasana preparatio: Side full-body Setubandhasana preparation; show small range, feet and slow descent.
messages.Side hinge and rear view of pelvis, both: Side hinge and rear view of pelvis, both hands visible throughout; show toe-down exit before optional foot lift.
messages.Side one-leg preparation and exit; separ: Side one-leg preparation and exit; separate static labeled silhouette for paired-leg knowledge only. Never animate legs over the head or imply pregnancy suitability.
messages.Side real-time knee walk-back, brief hol: Side real-time knee walk-back, brief hold and hips-back exit; show palms and wall option. Never morph knees-down plank into Chaturanga.
messages.Side view of Dandasana with straight and: Side view of Dandasana with straight and softly bent knees, then a chair equivalent.
messages.Side view of Padahastasana preparation w: Side view of Padahastasana preparation with bent knees and chair; show controlled exit.
messages.Side view of Uttanapadasana preparation,: Side view of Uttanapadasana preparation, one bent knee at a time, then seated march.
messages.Side view of a short reverse-table lift: Side view of a short reverse-table lift with neutral neck, entry and exit; show the chair chest-opening as a separate alternative, not the same skill.
messages.Side view of blanket-supported Vajrasana: Side view of blanket-supported Vajrasana and equal-size chair demonstration, including exit.
messages.Side view of cushion-supported Shashanka: Side view of cushion-supported Shashankasana and side-by-side chair-rest choice.
messages.Side view of gentle single-leg Pavanamuk: Side view of gentle single-leg Pavanamuktasana, no knee force; side-lying alternative.
messages.Side view of small Ushtrasana preparatio: Side view of small Ushtrasana preparation and chair version; explicitly omit full backbend.
messages.Side view shows bent knees, hand support: Side view shows bent knees, hand support and a short reach, then controlled return.
messages.Side wall hinge then separately labeled: Side wall hinge then separately labeled floor route with bent knees; show hands and complete knee-down exit, no match-score overlay.
messages.Side-lying or seated rest as the same po: Side-lying or seated rest as the same posture, a universal duration, pregnancy clearance, personal suitability or camera assessment.
messages.Simply listen to the breath if humming i: Simply listen to the breath if humming is uncomfortable; no ear-closing hand position is required.
messages.Sit back on a stable chair with both fee: Sit back on a stable chair with both feet touching the floor and leave room around the arms.
messages.Sit back toward the heels with chest and: Sit back toward the heels with chest and head supported and rise slowly with hand support.
messages.Sit by your familiar safe method. Rest h: Sit by your familiar safe method. Rest hands on thighs and use the backrest. If sitting or transfer needs help or is uncertain, choose reading and individual guidance instead of rehearsing it alone.
messages.Sit comfortably and first observe three: Sit comfortably and first observe three normal breaths with both nostrils open.
messages.Sit comfortably and take a natural inhal: Sit comfortably and take a natural inhale through the nose or mouth as needed.
messages.Sit forward from the backrest, feet flat: Sit forward from the backrest, feet flat, hands resting on the thighs. Find a comfortable tall seat as the neutral position.
Sit forward from the backrest, feet flat. Rest the forearms on the thighs or the desk.
messages.Sit in h04 easy seat or a chair and view: Sit in h04 easy seat or a chair and view labeled diagrams; keep your own legs uncrossed if that is more comfortable.
messages.Sit near a wall and turn onto the side b: Sit near a wall and turn onto the side before bringing legs up only as far as comfortable.
messages.Sit on a blanket with bent knees and pla: Sit on a blanket with bent knees and place hands on shins or a chair in front.
messages.Sit on a chair facing the camera with yo: Sit on a chair facing the camera with your arms crossed over your chest and your knees pointing forward. Turn your upper body to one side as far as is comfortable, return to centre, then turn the other way.
messages.Sit on a chair with feet apart if floor: Sit on a chair with feet apart if floor sitting or hip opening is uncomfortable.
messages.Sit on a chair, lift one arm only as com: Sit on a chair, lift one arm only as comfortable and bring the other hand toward the back waist.
messages.Sit on a folded blanket with shins loose: Sit on a folded blanket with shins loosely crossed, or on a chair with feet grounded.
messages.Sit on a folded blanket, bend knees a li: Sit on a folded blanket, bend knees a little and place hands beside the hips.
messages.Sit on a low firm blanket, legs forward: Sit on a low firm blanket, legs forward and knees comfortably bent. A prepositioned horizontal bolster beneath knees/thighs takes weight without forcing knees straight. Heels rest on the floor. Keep hands beside you on the floor; do not reach for toes.
messages.Sit sideways onto the blanket first, the: Sit sideways onto the blanket first, then bring the legs in front without locking the knees.
messages.Sit supported on the chair with feet on: Sit supported on the chair with feet on the floor/a support.
messages.Sit supported or lie comfortably; allow: Sit supported or lie comfortably; allow the inhale and exhale to arrive at their own pace.
messages.Sit supported, place one hand lightly on: Sit supported, place one hand lightly on the lower ribs and observe a few natural breaths.
messages.Sit tall on a chair or blanket and place: Sit tall on a chair or blanket and place hands loosely on thighs.
messages.Sit upright with legs extended without f: Sit upright with legs extended without forcing knees flat.
messages.Sit with back support and release the sh: Sit with back support and release the shoulders; this is attention training, not maximum lung filling.
messages.Sit with feet supported and hold a long: Sit with feet supported and hold a long strap; this lesson teaches arms, not the full crossed-leg Gomukhasana.
messages.Sit with knees bent and hands behind on: Sit with knees bent and hands behind on stable floor; point fingers to a comfortable direction.
messages.Sit with knees bent, feet flat roughly h: Sit with knees bent, feet flat roughly hip width and palms behind the hips in a comfortable direction.
messages.Sitting back toward the heels, chest or: Sitting back toward the heels, chest or head support and padding for knees and ankles.
messages.Skip prone lying in pregnancy or if it f: Skip prone lying in pregnancy or if it feels uncomfortable; use side lying or a chair. Prone abdominal contact is not a general pregnancy option; observe when personal suitability is uncertain.
messages.Slide one hand beside the chest and roll: Slide one hand beside the chest and roll gently to the side; pause before pushing up to sit.
messages.Solid non-wheeled observation/rest chair: Solid non-wheeled observation/rest chair only; not Yin movement.
Someone says, “I must never move in Yin.” Explain the right to leave in your own words. For symptom-free distraction return to ordinary breathing; if you deliberately slowed it, end observation, return to ordinary breathing and check a brief observation again. Remove “more sensation = better” from your progress criteria.
messages.Something unexpected happened while star: Something unexpected happened while starting the camera. Try again.

messages.Spend about a minute on each area, resti:
Spend about a minute on each area, resting whenever attention or breath feels strained.

Common mistake: Attention to three areas is mistaken for forcing breath into compartments. Correction: Observe where breathing is noticed without forcing separate compartments.

Use shorter attention periods and then return to ordinary awareness.

messages.Stand about {min}–{max} cm from the came: Stand about {min}–{max} cm from the camera.
messages.Stand beside a wall with both feet groun: Stand beside a wall with both feet grounded; keep the lower hand on support when balance needs it.
messages.Stand facing the camera with your hands: Stand facing the camera with your hands on your hips. Lift one foot off the floor and hold as steady as you can for up to 30 seconds. Put the foot down if you need to.
messages.Stand facing the camera, feet hip-width: Stand facing the camera, feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides. Slide one hand down the side of your leg, bending sideways as far as is comfortable. Return upright, then repeat to the other side.
messages.Stand facing the camera. Step forward in: Stand facing the camera. Step forward into a lunge, lowering your back knee toward the floor while keeping your torso upright. Push back to standing.
messages.Stand for three easy breaths, step away,:
Stand for three easy breaths, step away, then return twice and compare the feeling.

Common mistake: Knees lock or toes grip to imitate a still demonstration. Correction: Distribute contact under both feet without locking the knees.

Compare a supported stance with a lightly supported stance using the same foot spacing.
messages.Stand in a comfortable hip-width base ne: Stand in a comfortable hip-width base near the verified wall; knees not pushed backward, head above torso, eyes forward. Keep one palm at the wall if that support is familiar and needed.
messages.Stand near a wall with feet hip width; p: Stand near a wall with feet hip width; place palms at the back of the pelvis or keep one hand on support.
messages.Stand next to a wall; shift weight into: Stand next to a wall; shift weight into one foot and place the other toes on the floor.
messages.Stand side-on to a wall or with a chair: Stand side-on to a wall or with a chair beside you. Step the feet apart a little less than leg length; turn the right foot out and the left foot slightly in, heels roughly in line.
messages.Stand side-on to the camera with hands o: Stand side-on to the camera with hands on your hips. Push your hips backward and fold forward while keeping your back flat, then return upright.
messages.Stand side-on to the camera with your le: Stand side-on to the camera with your legs straight. Bend forward from the hips and reach toward your toes. Go only as far as is comfortable, hold two seconds, then stand up slowly.
messages.Stand side-on to the camera, feet should: Stand side-on to the camera, feet shoulder-width apart, arms forward. Squat as low as you comfortably can, hold for two seconds, then stand back up.
messages.Stand side-on to the camera. Let your ar: Stand side-on to the camera. Let your arms hang. Slowly raise the arm nearest the camera as high overhead as you can, keep the elbow straight, hold for two seconds, then lower.
messages.Stand side-on to the camera. Raise both: Stand side-on to the camera. Raise both arms straight overhead and keep them there. Squat as low as you can while keeping your arms up, then stand back up.
messages.Stand with feet about hip width apart an: Stand with feet about hip width apart and soften the knees; feel heel and forefoot contact.
messages.Standing, seated and kneeling poses — jo: Standing, seated and kneeling poses — joint angles and hold time
messages.Start and finish in mountain; practise e: Start and finish in mountain; practise each side before changing posture.
messages.Start facing a verified solid wall, feet: Start facing a verified solid wall, feet hip-width and palms at comfortable chest height, fingers up, elbows bent softly. Choose a distance at which upright contact is easy; feet stay fixed throughout this unit.
messages.Start from a04 with easy knees and both: Start from a04 with easy knees and both feet grounded. Keep needed wall support and choose a small range.
messages.Start in mountain beside a wall; step on: Start in mountain beside a wall; step one foot back and angle the rear toes outward enough for comfortable full-foot contact.
messages.Start in mountain, raise arms only comfo: Start in mountain, raise arms only comfortably, then hinge into h11 with hands on the secured chair or bent-knee floor support.
messages.Start in tabletop with a folded blanket: Start in tabletop with a folded blanket under the knees and two firm blocks beside the hands. Bring the right foot forward between the hands in small steps.
messages.Start in tabletop with padding under the: Start in tabletop with padding under the knees and two firm blocks or a stable chair seat within reach beside the hands. Choose the blocks or chair before moving, not during a transition.
messages.Start seated for two minutes, prepare th: Start seated for two minutes, prepare the joints, then rise slowly into mountain.
messages.Start upright near your planned wall sup: Start upright near your planned wall support. Keep feet on two comfortable parallel tracks rather than one tight line.
messages.Stay for a few ordinary breaths with wei: Stay for a few ordinary breaths with weight even between the feet. Dizziness or a pull behind the knees that does not settle ends the fold.
messages.Stay in mountain or observe with back di: Stay in mountain or observe with back discomfort, dizziness or uncertain balance. A smaller backbend is not automatically suitable for a health condition.
messages.Stay only within the shared time limit,: Stay only within the shared time limit, without sinking deeper during the hold. Pressure on the back kneecap means more padding or leaving; hip pinching or any stop signal ends the shape.
messages.Still needs a device pass: the permissio: Still needs a device pass: the permission dialog · the camera frame stream · landmark quality in real light · the calibration threshold (yaw ≤10°).
messages.Stillness does not forbid an adjustment: Stillness does not forbid an adjustment or early exit, and stronger sensation or longer time does not prove progress. Choose only the familiar accessible route; a knowledge route remains knowledge. Use the existing stop rules and leave early when needed, without waiting for the timer or creating symptoms.
messages.Stop and rest supported for pain, pinchi: Stop and rest supported for pain, pinching, dizziness, new tingling, unusual breathlessness or feeling unwell. Do not test a symptom by pushing through it. Sudden illness needs medical attention; persistent or recurrent symptoms need individual advice before resuming.
messages.Stop for dizziness, ear discomfort or br: Stop for dizziness, ear discomfort or breath strain.
messages.Stop for pain, dizziness or uncertainty: Stop for pain, dizziness or uncertainty about returning upright; do not force depth or retest symptoms.
messages.Stop for pain, dizziness, balance loss o: Stop for pain, dizziness, balance loss or an unfamiliar transfer. A pause or early finish is not a failed score.
messages.Stop for pain, dizziness, instability or: Stop for pain, dizziness, instability or uncertain return. Do not add repetitions to prove readiness.
messages.Stop for pain, instability or uncertaint: Stop for pain, instability or uncertainty about stepping back to neutral; do not practise an uncertain transfer repeatedly.
messages.Stop for pain, pinching, new tingling, d: Stop for pain, pinching, new tingling, dizziness, unusual breathlessness or feeling unwell. Use familiar supported rest, do not retest symptoms. Persistent/recurrent symptoms need individual advice; sudden serious illness needs prompt medical help.
messages.Stop if light-headed, breathless or anxi: Stop if light-headed, breathless or anxious; return to ordinary breathing.
messages.Stop if sharp pain, dizziness, or unusua: Stop if sharp pain, dizziness, or unusual breathlessness appears.
messages.Stop if tempted to test an untaught floo: Stop if tempted to test an untaught floor transfer; put it in the teacher question list.
messages.Stop the study if fatigued. Do not test: Stop the study if fatigued. Do not test unfamiliar positions to fill the boxes.
messages.Stop the study if tired. Reading a pose: Stop the study if tired. Reading a pose name is not a reason to try it.
messages.Stop turning, rest supported or observe;: Stop turning, rest supported or observe; seek individual advice if symptoms persist or recur. Contact shows the chosen base was maintained, not spinal alignment, injury status or medical suitability.
messages.Stop writing when fatigued. Mark an unce: Stop writing when fatigued. Mark an uncertain transfer as a teaching question rather than adding it.
messages.Straighten gently and step forward to th: Straighten gently and step forward to the same upright stance. Pause, then reverse feet for the left-forward side if suitable. Return upright before ending.
messages.Straighten gently, lower arms and turn b: Straighten gently, lower arms and turn both feet forward before stepping in or changing sides.

messages.Study seated; the map can be read withou: Study seated; the map can be read without any movement.

messages.Study the idea, explain it in your own w: Study the idea, explain it in your own words, then compare. No movement or equipment is needed. These reading activities do not complete a full course or approve physical technique.
messages.Supine and abdominal-loading restriction: Supine and abdominal-loading restrictions, including pregnancy-related limits, require a different personal plan; chair observation is available. messages.Take five natural breaths, then stretch:
Take five natural breaths, then stretch legs out and compare sides.

messages.Take one short step back with the left f: Take one short step back with the left foot; the right foot is now forward. Bend the front knee slightly in the direction of its foot while keeping the trunk upright.
messages.Take three comfortable breaths, then cho:
Take three comfortable breaths, then choose a chair rest for comparison.

Common mistake: Child rest compresses the abdomen or strains the knees. Correction: Select a rest that leaves the abdomen and breathing comfortable.

Compare supported child rest with chair rest instead of increasing the fold.
messages.Take three easy breaths per side, once o:
Take three easy breaths per side, once or twice.

Common mistake: The thigh is pulled against the abdomen beyond comfort. Correction: Bring one thigh towards the trunk only as far as the abdomen stays comfortable.

Compare a light hand-supported release with a smaller unsupported leg movement.

messages.Vinyasa here means intentionally connect:
Vinyasa here means intentionally connecting selected yoga shapes, transitions and attention with an unforced breath. It does not mean compulsory fast exercise or a compulsory plank–Chaturanga–upward-dog cycle. Yoga has Indian philosophical roots and extends beyond exercise. This original adapted pathway is a bounded introduction to Vinyasa learning, not a traditional fixed series or the entire Vinyasa domain. A supported standing route is the initial movement endpoint; the floor branch is explicitly knowledge-only pending individual instruction. Ten study units organize different decisions, not ten ticks that prove completion. [S1,S2,S3]

Know h01/h02 boundaries and natural breathing, h03 comfortable standing, h05 small joint preparation, h11 supported hinge and h35 unhurried transitions, or equivalent independently explained preparation. Reading/completion records are not proof. Before choosing movement, explain setup, demonstrate only familiar comfortable movements already learned, and identify a supported rest/exit. If standing, hand support, stepping or returning upright is unfamiliar or unsuitable, use written observation and seek qualified instruction; the chair pathway is a separate option, not evidence of standing ability. No full-Hatha completion or floor ability is imposed. Never stand from an unfamiliar floor position to follow this document.

Prepare afresh every session and after interruptions. Use a firm nonslip surface, clear foot space and a solid stationary wall, not glass, a door, heater or furniture that can move. Test light palm contact upright without leaning body weight into an unverified surface. A rest chair must not swivel, roll, rock or slide; both feet reach the floor. Keep eyes open. Wear clothing that permits movement; ordinary comfortable room temperature. Choose observation whenever setup is uncertain. For pregnancy, injury, balance problems or other health limits, ask the relevant health professional and qualified yoga instructor about individual suitability; this text cannot supply that assessment. [S2,S7]

Breathe naturally without holding, force, deliberate throat constriction or required count. An inhale/exhale cue is an optional attention invitation: if breath ends before movement, pause or breathe again; never race, prolong or hold breath to finish. Movements may take several breaths. Use a small comfortable range, soft elbows/knees and no end-range demand. Pain, pinching, new tingling, dizziness, unusual breathlessness or feeling unwell means stop, use the already familiar supported rest and do not retest the symptom. Sudden serious illness requires prompt medical help; recurrent/persistent symptoms require individual advice before restarting. Only a symptom-free setup/coordination error may receive one smaller retest. Stop cues and the one-retest limit are conservative author rules, not a diagnostic tool or evidence of safe technique.
